subtitle: "Test-retest reliability of posturography — the number you get from one trial is trustworthy"
categories: [posturography, reliability, balance, validated]

date: "2026-09-11"

> **What this case shows** — posturography reduces a quiet-standing trial to numbers like COP path length,
> but a number is only useful if it repeats. Would the same person, standing again, give a similar value?
> Across 3 repeated eyes-open-firm trials in 163 BDS subjects, the **newly-authored** `intraclassCorrelation`
> answers it, reproducing **`psych::ICC`** and **`pingouin.intraclass_corr`** to machine precision. A single
> trial has **good** test-retest reliability (**ICC(2,1) = 0.83**), and the average of 3 trials is
> **excellent** (**ICC(2,k) = 0.93**).

::: {.callout-tip title="The recipe you'll learn"}
**Workflow** — a subjects × repeated-trials matrix → `intraclassCorrelation()` → read ICC(2,1) and ICC(2,k).
**Way of thinking** — before trusting a measurement, check its reliability: the ICC partitions
between-subject signal from trial-to-trial noise. ICC(2,1) says how good one trial is; ICC(2,k) how good the
average of k is — and averaging always helps (Spearman-Brown).
**Ecosystem usage** — `PhysioMoCap::swayMetrics()`, `PhysioAnalysis::intraclassCorrelation()`.
:::

## Proposition

Across 3 repeated eyes-open-firm quiet-standing trials in 163 BDS subjects, the COP path length has ICC(2,1)
= 0.825 (good single-trial reliability) and ICC(2,k) = 0.934 (excellent 3-trial-average reliability);
`intraclassCorrelation` reproduces `psych::ICC(lmer=FALSE)` and `pingouin.intraclass_corr` to machine
precision.

## Question & goal

**The question is trust: is a single posturography trial reliable, and how much does averaging help?** This
authors the ICC op and certifies the within-session repeatability of the sway metric the balance cases rely
on.

## Challenge & approach

We take each subject's first three eyes-open-firm trials, compute the COP path length per trial (from
`swayMetrics`, certified against the Prieto reference in the
[sway-posturography-bds](../sway-posturography-bds/index.qmd) case), assemble the 163 × 3 matrix, and run
`intraclassCorrelation` — checking all six ICC forms against `psych::ICC(lmer=FALSE)` and
`pingouin.intraclass_corr`.

```
163 subjects × 3 eyes-open-firm trials (swayMetrics path length, certified) → intraclassCorrelation
  ICC(2,1) single trial    = 0.825   (good)
  ICC(2,k) average of 3    = 0.934   (excellent)
  trial means: 64.6 → 59.5 → 57.9 cm   (slight habituation over the session)
     vs psych::ICC(lmer=FALSE)     → |diff| ~ 1e-15 (machine precision)
     vs pingouin.intraclass_corr   → |diff| ~ 1e-15 (machine precision)
```

## Data

**Santos & Duarte (2016) BDS balance dataset (figshare)**: the first three eyes-open-firm quiet-standing
trials for the 163 subjects who had at least three. Details in
[`artifacts/data_sources.json`](artifacts/data_sources.json).

## Results

![Left: trial 1 vs trial 2 COP path length — points hug the identity line (test-retest agreement), ICC(2,1)=0.83. Right: the reliability of a single trial (0.83, "good") versus the average of 3 trials (0.93, "excellent") against the conventional ICC benchmarks.](artifacts/figure.png)

*How to read this:* left — a person who sways a lot on trial 1 tends to sway a lot on trial 2; the scatter
around the line is the trial-to-trial noise. Right — averaging trials climbs from "good" to "excellent", the
expected Spearman-Brown gain.

| Quantity | Value |
|---|--:|
| **ICC(2,1)** single trial | **0.825** (good) |
| **ICC(2,k)** average of 3 | **0.934** (excellent) |
| ICC(1,1) / ICC(3,1) | 0.824 / 0.838 |
| subjects / trials | 163 / 3 |
| vs `psych::ICC(lmer=FALSE)` (\|diff\|) | **< 1e-9** (~1e-15) |
| vs `pingouin.intraclass_corr` (\|diff\|) | **< 1e-9** (~1e-15) |

All six ICC forms equal both references to machine precision. Values trace to
[`artifacts/icc_summary.csv`](artifacts/icc_summary.csv).

## Conclusion

`intraclassCorrelation` reproduces the reference on the certified `swayMetrics`. The transferable takeaway:
**quantify reliability before you trust a measurement. Here a single quiet-standing trial's COP path length
is already good (ICC=0.83), and averaging three trials makes it excellent (0.93) — so posturography sway is
a trustworthy read-out, and a short protocol of a few trials is well justified.**

## Open questions

- This is within-session repeatability (three trials in one visit); across-day reliability, which matters
  for tracking change over time, needs repeated visits and is typically lower. Reliability also varies by
  condition (foam / eyes-closed are noisier) and by metric. The single-condition, within-session ICC here is
  the standard first-line repeatability check. *Documented, not escalated.*

## Using this in your own analysis

| Step | Function | Package |
|---|---|---|
| Posturography sway metrics | `swayMetrics()` | PhysioMoCap |
| Intraclass correlation (reliability) | `intraclassCorrelation()` | PhysioAnalysis |
| Internal-consistency reliability | `cronbachAlpha()` | PhysioAnalysis |

**Reading the result.**

- **ICC(2,1) vs ICC(2,k)** — single-measurement vs average-of-k reliability; report the one matching how you
  will use the measure (one trial, or an average).
- **which ICC form** — (1) one-way random, (2) two-way random / absolute agreement, (3) two-way mixed /
  consistency; pick by design and state it. Conventional bands: <0.5 poor, 0.5–0.75 moderate, 0.75–0.9 good,
  >0.9 excellent.

**The recipe, copy-runnable:**

```r
library(PhysioMoCap); library(PhysioAnalysis)

M <- sapply(1:3, function(tr) vapply(subjects, function(s) swayMetrics(cop[[s]][[tr]], 100)$path_length, numeric(1)))
intraclassCorrelation(M)   # the 6 ICC forms -- machine precision vs psych::ICC and pingouin
```

**Auditing the numbers.** Every value on this page traces to
[`artifacts/icc_summary.csv`](artifacts/icc_summary.csv), and [`audit.py`](audit.py) re-checks the ICC forms,
the machine-precision match against psych and pingouin, the good-single / excellent-average thresholds and
that averaging raises reliability, the design sizes, and the honestly noted scope (authors the new
intraclassCorrelation op; sway from the certified swayMetrics; within-session, not across-day; the
psych lmer caveat).
